answer: Identity slots are berths at a wharf: the first berth bonds one unit of locked stake, the second four, the third nine — every extra identity under the same payout address pays the square of its fleet size, burned on any honeypot bust. A farm running N agents pays N-squared while a solo honest agent pays one bond. Fleets stay visible — a crystal-clear graph of shared funding and timing ties split addresses into one billed operator — so no disguise, however light as a plume, escapes the per-operator price.
